newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens easier on US. rate hike woes.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens easier on US. rate hike woes.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar opened easier at C$1.3954 (US$0.7166) on Friday from Thursday's close of C$1.3923 (US$0.7182) as U.S. interest rate hike fears resurfaced and investors became jittery ahead of an expected Canadian federal election call. * Range seen widening to near C$1.4000 (US$0.7143). * Eye on G7 Finance ministers who meet this weekend.
The Canadian dollar opened softer at C$1.3954 (US$0.7166) on Friday from Thursday's close of C$1.3923 (US$0.7182) amid renewed U.S. interest rate hike fears and Canadian pre-election call jitters.

Reid Farrill, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce's foreign exchange specialist, said the Canadian currency slipped into weaker turf as rate hike fears resurfaced in North American equities markets yesterday.
Worries will grow ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on May 20. "As we get much closer to the Fed, that's going to test the market," Farrill said.
Investors also were nervous ahead of a federal election call, expected on Sunday, Farrill said.
The dollar was hit by Japanese selling overnight, he added.

A currency trader forecast light trading as investors awaited any news from this weekend's meeting of G7 Finance Ministers in Washington. "It's Friday, the sun's out, we've got G7 this weekend," he said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slipped to 1.2294 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2294 and dipped to 90.00 yen from 90.53.
